key_insight: A learned convolution-based closure can predict atmospheric boundary-layer heat and momentum fluxes more accurately than a standard K-profile model while keeping the flux–profile relationship interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to improving coarse-resolution weather and climate models with a transparent parameterization that can better handle both unstable and stable boundary-layer regimes.
method: Train linearized convolution operators on LES data over homogeneous surfaces.
Use nondimensional mean temperature and velocity profiles as inputs to predict nondimensional heat and momentum fluxes.
Compare several first-order closure variants and select the best model by mean-squared error.
evidence_signal: The closure was trained and tested on high-resolution LES across multiple stability regimes and then verified in posteriori single-column simulations, where it remained stable and matched LES profiles closely.
watch_item: Performance depends on LES-trained regimes and idealized homogeneous-surface conditions, so transfer to complex terrain or strongly heterogeneous real-world settings may require further validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Flux Parameterization for the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
